content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to keep code readable as projects grow. This skill gives practical clean code rules for names, functions, comments, errors, and formatting.
actual_capabilities: Explains naming patterns for variables, functions, and booleans.
Guides function design with single responsibility, fewer parameters, and early returns.
Shows when comments help and when clearer code is better.
Covers safer error handling by avoiding null return and null parameters.
Lists common code smells with practical cleanup directions.
Provides a checklist for reviewing code before commits.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not an automated static analyzer.
It does not execute code, run tests, or apply patches by itself.
It does not replace project-specific style guides or team conventions.
It focuses on general TypeScript-style examples, not every language ecosystem.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Identify naming, function design, error handling, and formatting issues before approval.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Legacy Module
use_cases.description: Break large functions into clearer steps and prioritize code smells for cleanup.

use_cases.title: Teach Clean Code Basics
use_cases.description: Use simple examples to explain readable names, focused functions, and useful comments.

prompt_templates.title: Review Names
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of variables and functions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the clean-code skill to review these variable and function names. Suggest clearer alternatives and explain each change briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor One Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the clean-code skill to refactor this function for single responsibility, early returns, and fewer parameters. Keep behavior unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Error Handling
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of null handling and failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the clean-code skill to review this error handling. Replace null-driven control flow with clearer results or exceptions where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Module Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit across a larger module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the clean-code skill to audit this module for naming, function design, comments, null handling, formatting, and code smells. Return prioritized changes.

output_examples.input: A function creates a user, sends email, logs activity, and returns the user.
output: Split user creation, email delivery, and logging into separate functions.
Name each operation after the action it performs.
Keep the original behavior while making the workflow easier to test.

output_examples.input: A review asks whether a boolean parameter should remain in a file creation function.
output: Replace the flag with separate functions for normal files and temporary files.
Use names that reveal the behavior without requiring callers to remember a boolean meaning.

output_examples.input: A team wants a checklist before merging a cleanup pull request.
output: Check that names are descriptive and searchable.
Confirm each function has one clear purpose.
Remove dead code and replace magic values with named constants.

best_practices: Provide the code section and explain the behavior that must stay unchanged.
Ask for small, reviewable changes instead of broad rewrites.
Compare suggestions with your team style guide before applying them.
anti_patterns: Do not rename public APIs without checking callers and documentation.
Do not split functions so far that the flow becomes harder to follow.
Do not add comments that repeat what clear code already says.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides clean code guidance and review suggestions that you can apply with your normal tools.

faq.question: Which code quality topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers names, functions, comments, error handling, formatting, code smells, and a pre-commit checklist.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it tied to one programming language?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript-style syntax, but the principles apply to many software projects.

faq.question: Can it replace automated linters or formatters?
faq.answer: No. Use it with linters, formatters, tests, and team review standards.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before code review, during refactoring, or when teaching maintainable coding practices.
